# Bind implementation documentation to committed source

## Decision requested

The owner approved this revised documentation-review policy on October13,2026. Verifier implementation may begin only after this approved verifier specification AND the separately specified policy-only FEAT-CICD-001 CODE implementation are actually on main. The policy-only branch has its own approved policy specification and five-task ready plan; the gated skill/template Markdown is process code, never a DOC exception. This approval does not approve or merge an incomplete AV implementation. Broad watcher coverage remains unchanged. Existing documentation review requires no new findings before merge but cannot use a feature SHA as a trunk baseline; squash also removes feature ancestry. A committed, exact source/body identity record resolves identity without claiming to authenticate an external CODE review.

## Local identity and external review are separate

The new record is a locally reproducible identity declaration. Its producer is `scripts/maintenance/doc_source_snapshot.py`; its verifier is in the same protected module, called by `scripts/maintenance/docs_audit.py`. Anyone may reproduce a record: it contains no signature, reviewer assertion, approval Boolean, issue-comment authority or fabricated authentication. Audit output says `implementation-source identity matched; external CODE review under existing rules; rollout pending`. It does not say `verified review`, and does not update the existing verified/trunk/deployment marker.

Authenticated external CODE review remains the repository's existing CODE-review prerequisite: current-head external review by the required reviewers, green required checks and resolved conversations, enforced through the normal merge process. The local CLI has no external-review trust anchor and cannot establish those facts. No new attestation service, API fetch, credential or network request is introduced. An identity-matched audit alone never permits merge; CODE reviewers must read the corresponding source and notes. Misstating review approval or deployed status is a review failure independently of identity matching.

## Exact record and committed-source contract

Only `docs/review-evidence/site-source-snapshot.json` is eligible. It lies outside watched runtime roots and outside `docs/product/`; records elsewhere do not affect findings. The producer reads committed trees, never uncommitted worktree content, and writes this sidecar after successful complete verification. CLI:

`python3 scripts/maintenance/doc_source_snapshot.py produce --policy-ref origin/main --source-ref HEAD --output docs/review-evidence/site-source-snapshot.json`

`python3 scripts/maintenance/doc_source_snapshot.py verify --policy-ref origin/main --source-ref HEAD --record docs/review-evidence/site-source-snapshot.json --max-seconds 5 --max-input-bytes 8388608 --max-entries 20000`

The verifier consumes the record from the committed `--source-ref` tree. Production derives eligibility rather than trusting a success flag: an initial-bootstrap tree uses the fixed protocol FEAT/spec; a DOC close-out uses independently measured exact two-path delta; an ordinary feature selects the single active committed ready plan for its actual named branch, whose FEAT/spec the existing gate resolves. Multiple/absent plans or competing routes are unavailable. The committed record stores that selected binding, but verification always independently checks the actual approved baseline/POLICY/SOURCE spec and note/delta predicates, including after squash without needing the branch name. Production callers cannot raise these fixed limits. Tests may lower them to exercise refusal. Both refs resolve to actual commits before enumeration; CLI arguments are literal argv, never shell fragments. No partial record is installed on failure. An existing output file is replaced atomically only after complete successful production.

Version1 has exactly these JSON keys: `version` (integer1), `context` (literal `implementation-source; rollout-pending` for declared-note/bootstrap, or `implementation-source; trunk-closeout-pending` for DOC close-out), `object_format` (`sha1` or `sha256`), `eligibility` (below), `policy` (below), `baseline` (below), `source_entries`, `source_identity_sha256`, `document_path` (literal `docs/product/03-SITE-TRACEABILITY.md`), `document_body_sha256`. Unknown/duplicate keys, invalid UTF-8, floats, extra JSON values and unsupported versions are refused. Canonical bytes are exactly the strict-UTF-8 encoding of Python json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False), followed by one LF, with only the admitted integers/strings/arrays/objects. Non-ASCII characters are literal UTF-8, not Unicode escapes; solidus is literal /, never escaped. Double quote and backslash are escaped; the short escapes for backspace, formfeed, newline, carriage return and tab are used, and other U+0000 through U+001F use lowercase four-digit Unicode escapes. No Unicode normalization occurs. Reject unpaired surrogates or other values that cannot encode as strict UTF-8. Re-encoding parsed record JSON must equal its original bytes exactly, so optional alternative escaping is refused. This same encoding defines every policy/source/body-record canonical hash input. Hashes use SHA256 lowercase64hex. Arrays are ordered by UTF-8 path bytes. Entries have exactly `path`, `mode`, `blob_oid`, `size_bytes`; OID width follows object_format, modes are JSON strings, only `"100644"`/`"100755"`, and size_bytes is a nonnegative JSON integer. Paths must be normalized repository-relative UTF-8, with no empty/dot/dot-dot components, leading slash, backslash, control bytes or duplicate entries. Symlinks/gitlinks and unreadable/missing objects in admitted scopes make proof unavailable; they are not skipped.

`policy` contains exactly `registry_path` (literal `docs/DOC_REGISTRY.md`), `registry_blob_oid`, `registry_mode` (literal string `"100644"`), `registry_type` (literal `blob`), `document_path`, `watch_paths`, `policy_identity_sha256`. The SOURCE tree registry must independently exist as the exact same blob OID, mode and type as the trusted POLICY tree registry. Any source-side registry edit, mode change, symlink/gitlink/replacement or deletion makes this route unavailable; there is no policy-change acceptance route. The registry path is the actual registry path already used by docs_audit, not an authored replacement. The trusted policy ref supplies that registry's complete unchanged SITE watch paths. `watch_paths` and their source enumeration are derived by the existing exact-path/descendant-prefix semantics, including every new descendant; no exclusions or authored subsets are accepted. Policy identity is SHA256 of canonical policy fields excluding its own hash. The verifier compares all fields to policy derived independently from the trusted ref. Changes to policy invalidate old records. The new protocol cannot narrow existing broad paths.

`baseline` contains exactly `main_commit_oid`, `source_entries`, `source_identity_sha256`, `document_body_sha256`, derived from the actual trusted policy tree at production time. The full-width `main_commit_oid` must resolve to an actual commit on current trusted main ancestry; its actual tree independently reproduces the baseline entries/body and approved spec. This ancestral main object survives squash and must be available in the fresh clone; no feature object is required. Its manifest uses the same entry schema and limits. These baseline facts are informational context after squash, not authority and not a substitute for the existing trunk marker. The branch acceptance route also requires `main_commit_oid` equal the resolved current trusted policy/main commit and compares all baseline fields to that independently enumerated tree and body. The full baseline is verified against its real ancestral main tree in every route, including landed acceptance; declared historical fields are never accepted unchecked. The landed acceptance route is available only if the record's complete source manifest and body also equal the independently enumerated current policy-ref tree and body; its older baseline is then explicitly labeled historical context. There is no caller-selected after-merge bypass. No unavailable baseline/feature commit is accepted as proof. There is deliberately no required feature SHA: authoritative source revision identity is `source_identity_sha256`, independently recoverable from the actual current commit's scoped entries. SHA256 is over canonical `{object_format,policy_identity_sha256,source_entries}`; the record's own path is outside these scopes. Git committed blob OIDs, modes and paths define content identity; inspect object existence/type/size through bounded Git plumbing and compare independently enumerated current entries. Do not buffer all186MiB of file contents or replace missing objects with declared hashes.

Reject replacement refs, grafts or other history/object rewriting that makes committed identity ambiguous; run Git with replacements disabled as an additional guard, not a substitute for refusal. Unsupported/shallow state that prevents resolving the policy/trunk marker or required objects is explicit unavailable state. Fresh-clone tests fetch enough main history for its existing trunk marker; they do not fetch the original feature SHA.

Document identity is SHA256 over strict-UTF-8 committed SITE text processed by the existing `_without_marker` normalization, then encoded UTF-8 without additional normalization. That existing normalization removes only marker-owned fields/anchor blank lines and preserves extra marker prose. The sidecar supplies all new protocol metadata; SITE receives no self-referential snapshot hash. All backend notes and every frontend/progress/evidence byte participate in body identity. Existing marker fields remain protected from feature edits. No record or verified status is accepted for a dirty SITE worktree during the audit.

## Exact document allowance

Approved capability specs may add the optional frontmatter field:

`site_source_notes: [CHARTS-02, JOURNAL-09]`

IDs are existing unique SITE Chain element IDs, sorted and duplicate-free. The gate reads this field only from the capability's immutable approved spec at its trusted merge base. Unknown IDs, duplicate fields or malformed declarations are refused; a feature cannot approve its own selector. Initial protocol implementation has no such declaration and edits no SITE bytes.

The only permitted new area is an appended `## Implementation-source notes` section with exactly the table header `| FEAT | Component | Backend source and tests (implementation only; rollout pending) |`. A feature may add/update only its own rows `(FEAT-ID, declared Component-ID)` there; each pair is unique and ordered. The exact delimiter is `|---|---|---|`; rows are single-line three-cell rows with no embedded pipe. Every declared component must have an added/updated own row relative to `baseline.main_commit_oid`, whose third cell begins `source_identity_sha256=<record current source_identity_sha256>; ` followed by nonempty backend/source/test prose. Because SITE and the sidecar are outside watched code paths, this source hash excludes both and introduces no cycle. Merely declaring IDs, unchanged notes, old/source-unbound note hashes or deleting a note cannot clear CODE drift. The producer reports the source identity first; update these declared cells, commit them, and rerun production for their exact final body before committing the sidecar. This preflight emits identity but never installs an eligible record until every note is bound. Empty/duplicate headings, structural/header changes, removed foreign rows and undeclared IDs are refused. Removing its existing note requires a declared ID as well, but removal alone supplies no eligible implementation-review record. Outside its allowed table cells, byte-for-byte SITE content is preserved; every existing Chain/checklist row and every frontend/progress/S/T/V/Te/deployment claim is untouched. Notes contain implementation-only prose and local repository backend/source/test references, not frontend screenshots, remote frontend implementation links or assertions of deployed availability. External CODE review enforces prose meaning; the gate enforces exact structural ownership and byte boundaries, not semantic authentication. Existing mixed backend/frontend Chain cells are therefore never opened by this allowance.

## Audit routing and bootstrap

`eligibility` has exactly `kind` (`declared-note`, `initial-bootstrap`, or `trunk-closeout-pending`), `feat_id`, `spec_path`, `spec_blob_oid`, `component_ids`. FEAT IDs, spec paths and OIDs must be canonical, not operator assertions. Independently read the actual approved immutable spec at `baseline.main_commit_oid`; FEAT must match its frontmatter, and its blob/mode100644/typeblob must equal both current trusted POLICY and SOURCE copies. Spec/current main/baseline must exist under the fixed limits; changing or self-approving the spec rejects proof. `component_ids` must exactly equal its sorted unique nonempty `site_source_notes` for declared-note, and be empty for the other routes.

**Declared-note:** branch acceptance requires all declared own SITE rows genuinely added/updated against baseline and bound to exact current source hash, with every non-owned byte unchanged. Landed acceptance independently rechecks the same note/spec/baseline facts AND requires complete current SOURCE manifest/body equal current MAIN manifest/body. It does not depend on a vanished feature SHA. A future changed-source branch requires its own current-main baseline, approved declaration and fresh bound note edits; a landed record is not a general opt-out.

**Initial-bootstrap:** exact FEAT `FEAT-CICD-001`, exact approved spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-feat-cicd-001-source-review-verifier.md`, empty note IDs, and SITE raw bytes identical to baseline. The initial branch route is available only while CURRENT trusted POLICY has no `scripts/maintenance/doc_source_snapshot.py`; SOURCE must add that file. In both branch and landed routes, all changed watched paths versus the independently verified ancestral baseline are a nonempty subset of exactly: `scripts/maintenance/doc_source_snapshot.py`, `scripts/maintenance/docs_audit.py`, `scripts/gate/spec_gate.py`, `tests/scripts/test_doc_source_snapshot.py`, `tests/scripts/test_docs_audit.py`, `tests/scripts/test_spec_gate.py`. No other watched change, initialization edit or unrelated runtime change qualifies. Ordinary scoped catalog/traceability/plan/sidecar changes remain under existing gate ownership. After squash, an initial-bootstrap record is accepted ONLY when its complete current SOURCE manifest/body equal current MAIN and its independently checked ancestral baseline lacked the verifier. A future branch changing even one watched file cannot reuse this route after the verifier is on main.

**DOC trunk-closeout-pending:** exact protocol FEAT/spec above, empty IDs, `baseline.main_commit_oid` equals current trusted main for the branch route, and complete watched SOURCE equals MAIN; registry/spec equality still holds. Independently derive the full committed changed-path delta against current MAIN, including additions/deletions/mode/type/path transitions. It must be a nonempty subset of exactly SITE plus the sidecar, both regular mode100644 blobs; SITE historical marker bytes are unchanged. No code/config/registry/policy/capability/spec/plan/initialization edit is admitted. This narrowly lets a separately reviewed DOC close-out commit publish genuinely checked main/staging SITE body evidence before a later trunk stamp; output is `implementation-source identity matched; external CODE review under existing rules; trunk documentation close-out pending`, not a claim of rollout status or deployed verification. Actual CODE reviews still assess the supplied source/body/deployed evidence. The record authenticates none of it. Landed pending acceptance requires complete SOURCE/BODY equal MAIN and independently rechecks the same two-path-only delta and unchanged historical marker against its actual ancestral baseline. This route cannot clear any new CODE drift because SOURCE must equal MAIN in full watched scope. A caller-supplied kind, Boolean, branch name or flag cannot override these independently measured predicates. Plan-done is a separate DOC commit under existing rules.

For SITE only, first run ordinary marker predicates and the original source/body drift measurement. A valid ordinary verified current-trunk marker with known date/Against and zero source AND body drift is terminal and takes precedence: retain normal audit checks, emit no rollout-pending/provenance requirement, and ignore any obsolete sidecar. Missing sidecar is legal on this terminal route. This is not inferred from a record, and a marker with unknown/nontrunk/invalid identity or unresolved drift cannot retire it.

Otherwise, only a completely valid matching record with one of the exact eligible routes below may replace the two drift questions `check_changed_since` and `check_doc_changed_since` with explicit identity-matched context. Missing/invalid/mismatched/ineligible records retain original findings and add a provenance finding when the identity route is needed. No declaration or unchanged notes cannot suppress watched-source drift. Ordinary marker shape/date/unknown/ancestry checks, bad references, incorrect descriptions, missing tests and every other audit check still run. Existing `Against` remains a genuine trunk baseline; this feature never stamps an unavailable feature SHA, moves Last reviewed, marks deployed verification or suppresses marker findings. Other documents retain original behavior. `--stamp --verify` remains trunk-only and gains no branch-stamping exception.

Stage1: owner approval received October13; publish the separate policy-only approved spec alone on main. Its named FEAT-CICD-001 CODE branch and five-task ready plan then change the two gated skill/template Markdown files and own scoped delivery records only, with actual unchanged BASE gate, existing required checks, no-new actual audits and normal external CODE review. It adds no verifier/SITE/sidecar/runtime/test/watcher change and does not require future verifier tests to close. Separately publish this approved verifier spec alone on main. Only after both real policy CODE and this real approved verifier spec are on main may Stage2 open. There is no self-prerequisite and no DOC exemption for gated policy. Existing approved specs stay immutable. No sibling unmerged code is copied or branch stacked.

Stage2: one CICD implementation PR changes the protected producer/verifier, auditor, gate ownership checks and suites, plus its permitted catalog/traceability/plan and the sidecar. It edits no SITE content, registry watcher or pinned workflow. Thus the unchanged BASE product-scope gate has no new SITE edit to reject. The actual proposed HEAD auditor may evaluate only the exact initial-bootstrap identity record for the unchanged SITE body against allowlisted new committed protocol source, while trusted policy lacks the verifier; branch-versus-main no-new comparison is performed with actual CLIs, not a fabricated trusted BASE verdict. This is the existing branch-audit execution model, explicitly limited to this approved protocol introduction. All actual BASE gate checks, unchanged BASE suite, four-seat review and complete affected suites must pass; no exception to no-new findings or required checks is authorized. If actual evidence cannot satisfy this sequence, stop and return to owner with a separate concrete policy decision; do not self-waive it.

Stage3: only after Stage2 is on main may other capability implementation branches use the now-trusted approved-spec SITE-note allowance. Their records additionally require the exact approved FEAT/spec binding and actual source-bound declared own note updates, and bind exact source and entire body; later unrelated watched-code or body edits invalidate the record and require reproduction and current-head CODE review. After each squash, a fresh main clone verifies identity independently of feature ancestry. Separate DOC main/staging close-out truthfully updates the historical trunk marker and deployed evidence only after actual checks; a matching source record never completes that close-out.

Stage4 terminal close-out, following existing two-phase stamp guards: (a) when only the marker needs updating, on a separate DOC branch verify current committed main source/body/staging evidence, use existing trunk-only `--stamp --verify`, and delete the sidecar in the same DOC commit; terminal ordinary predicates must pass without consulting it. (b) if SITE body must first change, a separate DOC-only body-update PR carries a newly produced `trunk-closeout-pending` record and real evidence; it keeps the old marker, passes actual branch/main audit through that exact no-CODE-change route, completes normal reviews and merges. Then fetch that actual main commit containing the body, re-read/check source/body/staging, and on a second DOC-only PR use existing `--stamp --verify` against this genuine trunk revision and remove the record. The existing stamp refuses dirty/uncommitted body or a body not at its selected trunk baseline; never stamp a feature SHA or declare either first-stage pending state terminal. Commit/audit controls prove final marker-only/record-deletion state has zero original source/body drift and no new provenance finding. Deployment claims come solely from genuine close-out evidence, not any identity record.

## Bounds and acceptance controls

One monotonic deadline starts before record/ref/policy/object setup and ends after parsing, enumeration, object metadata checks, canonical identity/body calculation and final verdict/output. All Git child processes share the remaining budget; deadline refusal terminates/reaps them. No background or partial-success path survives a timeout. There is no authentication/network I/O. Admission ceilings are combined across current and baseline manifests: at most20000 entry records; at most8388608 input bytes across record, Git listings and object metadata (each actual byte read counts, including repeated reads); committed SITE body also counts. EVERY actual policy/eligibility input byte also counts, including each registry, selected plan, current/baseline/POLICY/SOURCE spec and initializer/policy blob read, not just object metadata; repeated reads are charged again. Check actual object sizes against remaining allowance before bounded content reads, and retain one shared parsing/enumeration deadline. Oversized trusted registry/spec/plan controls must refuse before unbounded buffering or parsing. Stream bounded reads and reject before exceeding either ceiling. Eight-MiB ceiling is a deliberate fail-closed capacity limit, not an assertion that every 20000-entry input fits. Output records must also fit the same ceiling before installation.

Actual CLI verdict JSON reports success/unverified, eligible route or terminal ordinary route, entry count, actual counted bytes, source/policy/body identities, elapsed seconds and refusal reason. Cold/ordinary actual runs must complete within5seconds on the normal runner; unsupported or slower input stays unverified. Existing tree approximately1519entries/186MiB of blobs is context, not measured performance evidence. New Cloud Run/jobs/schedulers/vendor/API/auth calls: zero; existing public hosted-runner allocation incremental billed cost zero. Full-render60seconds/512MiB and registry285second limits remain independent.

Tests must use actual producer and consumer CLIs, actual branches, squash and fresh clone. Accepted control is a real record produced for real committed source/body. Refused controls mutate committed source mode/blob/path/add/delete or notes/body/policy after production; corrupt/drop producer output; provide well-formed wrong identities; exceed record/listing/body/entry/deadline limits; introduce unsupported path/type/replacement state; or change another feature's/undeclared/frontend bytes. Every refused control checks nonzero/unverified or actual retained findings, with no successful placeholder return. Producer nonzero, timeout or partial output must leave no new installed record. Required actual failure controls start both with no output and with a valid installed sidecar; the absent case remains absent, and the previously valid installed bytes remain byte-for-byte intact after EVERY failure. Output is never opened/truncated/deleted before complete successful production; stage only a temporary file and atomically replace on verified success. Tests must also prove the failed attempt cannot corrupt or remove the last valid record. Exact matching records do not authenticate external reviewers or certify deployment: tests verify those labels and preserve an unrelated audit finding.

The eight acceptance items above must additionally exercise actual missing/empty declarations, unchanged/wrong-source notes, wrong FEAT/spec/self-approved spec, initial-bootstrap unrelated-file change, bootstrap reuse after main verifier installation, SOURCE/POLICY registry content/mode/type inequality, ancestral baseline/spec unavailability, and DOC retirement. Pair each refusal with its actual accepted branch/landed/terminal control. Real DOC close-out tests perform the body-publication squash and later current-trunk stamp/removal; premature deletion with stale marker, new CODE changes in pending close-out, body changes after stamp and unsupported record state retain ordinary findings. No additional authentication calls, broad waiver or weakened watcher is introduced.

## Required format, policy-input and dirty-worktree controls

These controls are part of the existing eight acceptance items and fourteen-task implementation plan, not a separate scope. Actual producer/verifier/audit/BASE-gate accepted controls must run in BOTH a default SHA-1 repository and a real `git init --object-format=sha256` repository. Pair SHA-256 acceptance with malformed and wrong-width OID refusals; no simulated object-format success is evidence. A committed `scripts/café.py` path must produce literal UTF-8 canonical JSON and reproducible identity; otherwise-equivalent Unicode-escaped or escaped-solidus records must fail canonical-byte comparison. Independently test oversized registry, selected plan and each required spec revision against the combined eight-MiB ceiling; genuine accepted controls below the limit use the same real commands.

After producing and committing a valid matching record, separately modify SITE only in the index and only in the unstaged worktree, including staged content restored in the worktree. The actual docs-audit CLI must retain dirty-state/provenance findings and emit neither record identity-matched nor verified status in both cases. Clean controls with the identical committed record must pass the eligible route. Committed-only mutation tests do not satisfy these dirty-state controls. Implementation must examine both index-versus-HEAD and worktree-versus-index before choosing either identity or terminal verified routes.

## No lazy-fetch acceptance boundary

Before object-inspecting Git plumbing, refuse partial-clone/promisor repository state, including configured extensions.partialClone or promisor remotes, rather than permitting lazy object retrieval. All producer/verifier Git children additionally disable lazy fetch through a supported verified Git capability; unsupported versions or ambiguous repository configuration are unavailable. Preserve inherited credentials/proxy/CA and never make a network/authentication call. Actual tests create a partial clone with a missing watched blob and a real promisor remote instrumented to record/reject access. The real producer/verifier/audit commands must refuse while the remote-access sentinel remains absent. An otherwise identical complete ordinary repository is the accepted control; a demonstrated unprotected Git lazy fetch verifies that the instrumented remote would detect access. Ordinary missing-object or timeout-only controls do not satisfy this requirement. These are additional cases in the existing Git-state task/acceptance, not a new scope or resource allowance.
